pass_b_english: XV. And here too rules are to be noted. 1. Between the testimony and phrases of Scripture and between the testimony and phrases of the Church one must accurately and carefully distinguish — as: the bread which we break is the communion of the body of Christ ([[1 Corinthians 10:16 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 10:16]]); and the bread is the body of Christ. The former is Scripture's phrase, the latter the Church's. Both indeed true: yet the former proper, the latter improper.

2. In public testimony, although there is one and the same truth, yet there is not always one and the same authority. For greater is the authority of the Apostolic Symbol, but lesser that of the Augsburg, Gallican, Helvetic, Belgian, Anglican confession and the like. 3. Public testimony, other things equal, is deservedly to be preferred to private. Thus the confession of the whole Church surpasses the confession of some one doctor — even if there as here there is one truth.

4. Of testimonies taken from the fathers the unique norm and touchstone is Sacred Scripture. Thus Augustine, On the Unity of the Church chapter 5: It is not to be heard in the Church, he says: I say this, you say this — but the LORD says this. Worthy of observation here too is the warning of Nicephorus Gregoras, Roman or Byzantine History book 10, page 235: Moreover, he says, it is also worth knowing that the writings of the holy fathers are not to be understood simply nor in one way. Of which some look to teaching and admonishing — are accommodated to teaching and admonishing, persons and times being considered, yet all religiously. For some contain decrees dogmatically; others praises encomiastically; others disputations combatively. Nor indeed are the ancients' disputations to be transferred elsewhere. For if someone fighting with enemies, and with whole mind intent on sword and shield, should strike down a fellow-soldier standing before his feet, neither is that to be thought a law, nor is he to be accused who did it, necessity drawing the thought from the struggle, by no means allowing that what was done should happen otherwise. Therefore neither is this to be so done, nor are praises to be used in place of laws. For art has given to those praising license to say anything. But those dogmas which they sanctioned and promulgated — in those alone it is right and safe to use them as canons and the plumbline of religion. Thus Nicephorus — which yet by our rule are always to be tested against Scripture's Lydian stone, as was demonstrated above.
source_text: XV. Sunt autem hic quoque notandae regulae. 1. Inter testimonium phrasesque scripturae & inter testimonium phrasesque Ecclesiae accurate & caute distinguendum est; ut, panis, quem frangimus, est communio corporis Christi 1. Cor. 10.v.16. Panis est corpus Christi. Illa scripturae, haec Ecclesiae phrasis est. Utraque vera quidem: illa tamen propria, haec impropria est. 2. In publico testimonio, quamvis una sit eademque veritas, non tamen semper una eademque est authoritas. Major enim est symboli Apostolici authoritas, minor vero confessionis Augustanae, Gallicae, Helveticae, Belgicae, Anglicanae & similium. 3. Publicum testimonium, caeteris paribus, privato merito est anteponendum. Sic, totius Ecclesiae confessio antecellit confessioni unius alicujus doctoris; etiamsi tam illic, quam hic una veritas. 4. Testimoniorum, quae a patribus sumuntur unica norma & fidius lapis est sacra scriptura. Sic Augustinus lib. de unitate Ecclesiae cap. 5. Non, inquit, audiendum in Ecclesia: haec dico, haec dicis: sed haec dicit DOMINUS. Digna quoque observatu hic est monela Nicephori Gregorae lib. X. historiae Romanae sive Byzantinae pag. 235. Caeterum, ait, illud quoque scire est opera pretium, non simpliciter, nec uno modo sanctorum patrum scripturas intelligendas esse. Quarum aliae didaskalikos kai parainetikos blepousi, ad docendum & monendum accommodate sunt personarum & temporum habita ratione, sed religiose omnia. Nam aliae dogmatikos, decreta continent, aliae enkomiastikos, laudationes, aliae agonistikos, disceptationes. Neque vero disceptationes Veterum alio transferendae sunt. Neque enim, si quis pugnans cum hostibus, & toto animo in gladium & clypeum intentus, commilitonem ante pedes stantem prostraverit, vel lex ea putanda est, vel is accusandus qui id fecit, cogitationem a lucta trabente necessitate, eo minime sinente ut id quod factum est, aliter fieret. Ergo neque hoc sic agendum est, neque laudationibus vice legum utendum. Ars enim laudantibus quidvis dicendi licentiam dedit. Quae vero dogmata sanxerunt & promulgarunt, in iis demum rectum & tutum est veluti canonibus & amussi religionis uti. Haec Nicephorus, quae tamen ex regula nostra ad lydium scripturae semper exigenda sunt, ut supra demonstratum est.
